editorial.evidence: Compared all 46 captured sections of the 15 Nov 2026 air-gapped capture against the earlier draft paragraph by paragraph. The draft had compressed the source heavily: it dropped the blast-radius section, the five-bucket failure taxonomy, the six technical-health metrics with calculations and alert rules, the risk register mitigations and triggers, the go/no-go gates and rollback triggers, the core-product standardisation category, the six weak-answer repairs, the answer-key evaluation table, the worksheet candidate scorecard, the 50-minute block contents, the piece-by-piece verifier walkthrough and the third SignatureError test, and it gave the three section-4 figures one shared caption. Those are restored in the walkthrough (new step 8 for metrics and ownership), deep dives and Practice; the six architecture-changing questions now say what each answer changes, and the question-tree, happy-path and failure-overlay figures each sit beside their own explanation. Practice grew from six to sixteen reveals covering every worksheet section, the four follow-ups, the mandatory drill, the 477 challenge, the dashboard question, weak/average/strong answers and the spoken summaries; the implementation-exercise answer is labelled authored. Added caveats are labelled: HMAC is symmetric, VerifiedManifest is only shallowly frozen, ValidationError is unused and both sketches do not prove transitive closure. No RAG-specific material from the reference case was transplanted. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): sketch 2's comment 'Validate the closure of the bundle' over a loop that only hashes listed artifacts → comment now reads 'Verify every listed artifact is present and unaltered', and the prose says closure needs its own preflight; the 10x ceiling 'about 4,760' → stated as 400,000 / 84 = 4,761.9, rounded up to 4,762 replicas, without commentary on the source's rounding.
